comparator.name: Mathematics (Wiskunde)
comparator.academicYear: Prospective official year-one and year-two 2026–27 and year-three 2027–28 pages, checked 2026-09-25; course offerings and elective restrictions may change
comparator.route: Ordinary 180-EC Mathematics bachelor, first-listed Wiskunde leerlijn, 9 EC year-one free choice and 36 EC later free choice
comparator.sourceNotes: The ordinary bachelor is 180 EC over three 60-EC years. Year one has 51 EC required, including two calculus units, two linear-algebra units, analysis, probability, group theory, introductory mathematics, programming and data science; another 9 EC is genuinely free. Year two has 12 EC universal compulsory courses (ethics/philosophy, writing, multivariable analysis), and the first-listed Mathematics (Wiskunde) line adds 18 EC prescribed differential equations, rings/fields and topology. Over years two and three the selected line also requires 18 EC line-restricted mathematics electives and 12 EC further second-/third-year mathematics electives, total 48 EC in the line. The official elective page says choose at least one of its 3-EC courses in year two; the first-listed Informatietheorie en Codes is selected as 3 EC of the supplementary mathematics block. Year three additionally requires 3 EC seminar, 6 EC modelling practicum, 3 EC portfolio and 12 EC mathematics thesis. The remaining 36 EC across years two and three is genuinely open; an education minor is only one optional use. The 9/9 restricted electives, 3/9 supplemental mathematics and 18/18 free-space split between years two and three produces a coherent 60+60+60 representative pacing, rather than asserting those elective choices are prescribed course-by-course. Published line lists govern eligible subjects and the student catalogue/OER governs exact elective conditions. The public year pages are indicative prospective offerings, not a guarantee of an individual timetable.

routeSelection.route: Ordinary 180-EC Mathematics bachelor, first-listed Wiskunde leerlijn, 9 EC year-one free choice and 36 EC later free choice
routeSelection.basis: The first-listed Wiskunde line is chosen from the university’s three formal lines (Wiskunde, Toegepaste Wiskunde, Kansrekening en Statistiek) without selecting for UCR fit. It uses the official required subjects and the correct 18+18+12 EC line architecture. Unrestricted choice remains generic; the 3-EC second-year supplementary elective is selected from the official 3-EC list to respect its explicit minimum.

exception.reason: This mathematics degree requires a broad proof-based progression: 51 EC in a dense first-year mathematical core, an additional required 6 EC multivariable analysis and 18 EC in differential equations, rings/fields and topology in the selected line, then 30 EC more upper mathematics (18 restricted line electives and 12 additional mathematics electives), plus a 12-EC independent mathematics thesis, seminar and modelling work. UCR offers introductory and applied mathematics, statistics, programming and data science but lacks sustained stand-alone real/complex analysis, abstract algebra and topology at the required depth. Substituting AI and data-science courses for the upper mathematical sequence would misrepresent the defining Mathematics identity, despite substantial overlap in applied computational methods.
exception.curriculumContext: The selected first-listed line is Mathematics, not the differently required Applied Mathematics or Probability and Statistics lines. Year 1=51 EC compulsory+9 EC free; years 2–3=12 EC common year-two courses+48 EC Mathematics line (18 prescribed, 18 restricted choices, 12 supplemental mathematics)+24 EC year-three fixed seminar/practicum/portfolio/thesis+36 EC genuinely free. The 3-EC first-listed course from the dedicated elective page meets its second-year selection rule. Exact elective allocations by year are illustrative and must respect the current online catalogue/OER. Public year-one/two pages give 2026–27 and year-three gives 2027–28 indicative offerings.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows with descriptions, prerequisites, profiles and planned terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods introduces calculus and linear algebra; DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH312 Linear Systems, DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics and DISARIN212 Logic & Discrete Mathematics provide relevant but predominantly introductory or applied coverage. DISGATE101 Programming and DISDATA111/211/311 add computational/data-science methods. There is no dedicated UCR sequence in real and complex analysis, rings and fields, topology, functional analysis, number theory or mathematics-specific independent thesis sufficient for this 180-EC route. Cross-disciplinary electives cannot fill the restricted 48-EC Mathematics line without changing the subject of the comparison.
